The Green Fields of Woodford

This jig is often associated with Bronx fluter Jack Coen, who is originally from Woodford, East Galway. Another E. Galway flute player Sean Moloney also recorded it citing his father Eddie Moloney as the source.

The Green Fields Of Woodford, X:5

I learned this version from the playing of Sorcha Costello at the 2017 Feakle Fiddle Festival. It’s a beautiful tune and she played it in A, which I think gives it a bit of an extra lift. She’s a wonderful player, and an excellent teacher too. Thank you Sorcha.

Re: The Green Fields Of Woodford

The Humours of Ross was a title that Michael Tubridy gave to Breathnach for the setting in CREII #47. Breathnach’s setting was from Eddie Moloney in Kinvara in 1960. That setting is different to the Humours of Ross https://thesession.org/tunes/7427, which also comes from the Moloney family.

The Green Fields Of Woodford, X:15

Here’s a setting with basic chords. Playing a D7 over the first halves of bars 1 and 5 is a possibility too, i.e. “D7”dBA “G”G2D.

If it’s played as the last tune of a set, a G chord could hang on for the whole final bar, though I prefer something like an ending tag of “G”GED “D7”DEF||“G”G6|] to resolve it back to G.

↳ Posted by benhockenberry on August 14th, 2025.

Re: The Green Fields Of Woodford

Per Sean Moloney, this is a composition of Tommy Whelan and called Mol Kelly’s Old Sow. Whelan’s Old Sow is also included in the book Sean put together, but not named as such:
https://tommywhelan.com/assets/downloads/book/Compositions_of_Tommy_Whelan.pdf
